target_customer: Music producers, DJs and fans who remix songs and make samples
problem: Producers need unique samples and fans want to remix favorite songs; Soundry offers generative tools (Groove for remixes, Sample Planet for samples).
business_model: Consumer and prosumer subscription (GeekWire reported $10 a month for sample packs)

founders.name: Mark Buckler
previous_startups: Codex Collective (live music event production company)

founders.name: Justin Parus
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page and launch post.

founders.name: Diandre Ruiz
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page; professional musician.

competitors.what: Sample library marketplace the YC page contrasts with Soundry

competitors.name: Suno
competitors.what: AI music platform the YC page contrasts with Soundry

competitors.name: Boomy
competitors.what: AI music platform the YC page contrasts with Soundry

technical_complexity.rationale: The CEO trained a model that decomposes songs into lyrics, melody, voice and instrumentation; text to sample generation needs research grade audio ML.

defensibility.rationale: Well funded AI music rivals and licensing risk; no proprietary dataset is sourced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Splice later added generative tools per a 2025 article; no source ties that to Soundry's outcome.

market_need_then: Producers buy sample packs and fans love remixing; GeekWire (2024) covered the text to sample generator; demand evidence is thin.

branding.brand_signature: Two product brands: Groove (groove.fm) and Sample Planet (sampleplanet.fm)
branding.community_and_virality: A GeekWire article and EDM Honey covered the launch; directory listings describe a community sample library.

brand_strength.rationale: Product names Groove and Sample Planet are memorable and press covered the launch, but no mascot or community scale was found.

outcome_analysis: Soundry AI built generative music tools in Seattle and joined YC in Winter 2024, with Groove for remixes and Sample Planet for samples. The YC directory shows Inactive while the company site still shows a 2026 notice and lists supporters, so the status is conflicting and no shutdown cause is public. The funding evidence is a database-reported $500K plus GeekWire saying a seed round was close. No failure factors are assigned.
notes: Round rests on CB Insights alone. The company site lists a16z, Goodwater Capital and My Asia VC as supporters but gives no round, so they are not recorded as a round. GeekWire could not be opened (403); its seed comment came via a search snippet. Competitors come from the YC page contrast, which is undated; date set to batch time. Search tool reported Active status; the fetched YC page said Inactive.
